note: Named surfaces, so a caller asks for a kind of material rather than for numbers. The vocabulary is deliberately small: a name somebody can argue with beats a slider nobody can check.

recipes.name: crystal
recipes.description: clear faceted stone, like quartz or ice
recipes.why: Dielectric and smooth, transmitting most of what falls on it. Metal cannot transmit light at all, which is why a crystal marked metallic can never be made to read as one.

recipes.name: gemstone
recipes.description: cut gem, brighter and harder than crystal
recipes.why: A higher index bends light further, which is what makes a cut stone catch and throw it.

recipes.name: brushed-metal
recipes.description: worked metal with a directional finish

tones.note: Where a colour sits in value, so two parts painted the same hue can still be told apart. A sword's deep blue body and the bright stone at its throat are both blue.
